title: Sludge stack
notes: Cranked-amp rhythm guitar for a riff that leads the mix rather than sitting under a lead. Forked from brown-rhythm and moved toward chainsaw-chug on drive, but deliberately not onto it: the oscillator stays a saw, because this is an overdriven amp rather than a fuzz pedal, and a saw driven hard keeps a pick edge where a square smears into wool. Four moves from the parent. Input 1.7 -> 4.6 and preamp 0.5 -> 0.86, so the chug is saturated rather than crunchy. Tighten 170 -> 120: the low strings are let partly into the drive, enough to thicken the low mids, not enough to go woolly — between the brown rig's clean lows and the chainsaw's 160-on-a-square. Mids left in (+6.5) with the honk at 1.8 kHz rather than the 2.7 kHz rasp the chainsaw voices bump, which is the difference between a thick vintage stack and a buzzsaw. Cab rolled down to 3.9 kHz so the gain arrives as weight, not fizz. Width 0.78, because this tone is heard double-tracked; the lead pair sits inside it. Sum low (0.34) since all that gain arrives as level.
summary: Cranked-amp rhythm, mids in, lows half into the drive. A riff that leads the mix — boss fights, sludge. Saw edge, not chainsaw wool.
